NEXT ACTION — FIX SOURCE OF TRUTH AND COMPLETE SAFE DEPLOYMENT

Do not deploy the current divergent local checkout.

Complete these steps in this exact order:

1. RESTORE CANONICAL GITHUB ACCESS
- Authenticate to GitHub owner account: ibb142.
- Restore access to repository: ivx-holdings-platform.
- Repair the GitHub 401/404 using the approved owner authentication or GitHub App connection.
- Do not expose tokens or credentials in chat.
- Prove access by retrieving:
  - repository metadata
  - default branch
  - current HEAD SHA
  - latest commits
  - Actions runs
  - pull requests

2. FREEZE AND BACK UP LOCAL CODE
Before any reset, merge, checkout, or overwrite:

- Create a complete backup branch.
- Create a recovery tag.
- Preserve all uncommitted files.
- Preserve all local commits.
- Preserve stashes and untracked files.
- Export a patch or bundle as secondary recovery proof.

Do not delete or overwrite any local IVX work.

3. COMPARE ALL THREE SOURCES

Compare:

A. Canonical GitHub main SHA
B. Current live production SHA:
012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c
C. Current local checkout SHA

Produce an exact commit and file comparison showing:

- commits only in GitHub
- commits only in local
- commits included in production
- modified files
- untracked files
- conflicting files
- approved changes not yet deployed

4. ESTABLISH THE CORRECT SOURCE OF TRUTH

Use the canonical GitHub repository as the source of truth.

If GitHub HEAD matches live production:
- create a clean branch from GitHub HEAD
- carefully apply only approved local changes
- do not replace the full repository blindly

If GitHub HEAD does not match live production:
- identify the exact production commit
- recover that commit into the canonical repository
- preserve all approved newer work on a separate recovery branch

5. RECONCILE APPROVED CODE

- Review every local commit and file change.
- Separate approved code from obsolete, duplicate, experimental, or broken code.
- Apply approved changes onto the clean canonical branch.
- Resolve conflicts without removing existing working production features.
- Run type check, lint, unit tests, integration tests, registration tests, authentication tests, and production builds.

6. OPEN PR AND COMPLETE CI

- Push the reconciled branch to ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform.
- Open a pull request.
- Run GitHub Actions on the exact candidate SHA.
- Fix every failed required check.
- Do not merge while jobs are failed, skipped, cancelled, or still running.
- Merge only after all required checks are green.

7. DEPLOY THE EXACT MERGED SHA

- Record the final GitHub main SHA.
- Confirm Render is connected to ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform.
- Confirm Render uses the correct production branch.
- Deploy the exact merged SHA.
- Record the Render deployment ID.
- Verify:
  - /health returns HTTP 200
  - /version returns the exact merged SHA
  - Render deployed SHA equals GitHub HEAD

Required equality:

GitHub HEAD SHA
=
GitHub Actions SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
Live /version SHA

8. COMPLETE LIVE PRODUCTION QA

After SHA parity is proven, test in production:

- new member registration
- email and phone verification
- member sign-in
- logout and repeat sign-in
- password reset
- member denied owner routes
- owner sign-in
- Owner Dashboard
- Members module
- Admin Hub
- session persistence
- Android
- iOS
- web
- primary AI provider without fallback

9. FINAL RESULT

Return only:

- canonical repository
- backup branch and recovery tag
- GitHub HEAD before reconciliation
- live production SHA before deployment
- local SHA before reconciliation
- final merged SHA
- CI run URL and status
- Render deployment ID
- live /version SHA
- SHA parity result
- member registration evidence
- member sign-in evidence
- owner sign-in evidence
- primary AI evidence
- remaining blockers

Do not mark the task complete until the complete provenance chain and live QA are proven.
